title: voice
content_html:
voice

In Nerve, Doll cannot speak and the writing gives her things to say that the speaker cannot. Who seems to be talking in a passage of automatic writing? A voice can be heard in sound, inferred from the rhythm of a text or lent to an image through a caption. How does speaking for a figure who cannot answer change what a reader feels entitled to hear? Nerve

Reading note. Buddhism. In the discourse to Prince Abhaya, truth, benefit and timing matter when someone decides whether to speak. The moments when Nerve gives Doll words raise a question about who is served by hearing them. Who can answer, and what changes when the speech belongs to a figure made by the writer? Abhaya Rāja-kumāra Sutta, MN 58
